WITH production_files AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, s.file_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind = 'class'
    AND s.qualname LIKE '%.SQLDatabase'
    AND s.file_id IN (
      SELECT f.file_id
      FROM code.files f
      WHERE f.module NOT LIKE 'tests/%'
    )
),
connector_classes AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT class_symbol_id
  FROM production_files
),
class_methods AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS method_symbol_id,
         s.qualname AS method_qualname,
         s.file_id AS class_file_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind = 'method'
    AND s.qualname NOT LIKE '_%'
),
own_methods AS (
  SELECT cm.method_symbol_id,
         cm.method_qualname,
         cm.class_file_id
  FROM class_methods cc
  JOIN class_methods cm ON cm.class_file_id = cc.file_id
  WHERE cm.method_qualname NOT IN (
    SELECT s2.qualname
    FROM code.symbols s2
    WHERE s2.file_id = cc.file_id
      AND s2.kind = 'method'
      AND s2.qualname NOT LIKE '_%'
      AND s2.qualname != cm.method_qualname
  )
),
public_own_methods AS (
  SELECT method_symbol_id,
         method_qualname AS method_name,
         class_file_id AS class_symbol_id
  FROM own_methods
  WHERE method_name NOT LIKE '_%'
)
SELECT class_symbol_id,
       method_name
FROM public_own_methods
ORDER BY class_symbol_id,
         method_name;

request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
explanation: The query identifies production files with SQLDatabase subclasses, then finds methods directly defined in those classes (excluding inherited ones via NOT EXISTS). It filters to public methods (names not starting with underscore) and returns one row per (class_symbol_id, method_name). The column alias file_id was replaced with class_file_id to match the actual column name in code.symbols.

WITH production_files AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, s.file_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind = 'class'
    AND s.qualname LIKE '%.SQLDatabase'
    AND s.file_id IN (
      SELECT f.file_id
      FROM code.files f
      WHERE f.module NOT LIKE 'tests/%'
    )
),
connector_classes AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT class_symbol_id
  FROM production_files
),
class_methods AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS method_symbol_id,
         s.qualname AS method_qualname,
         s.file_id AS class_file_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind = 'method'
    AND s.qualname NOT LIKE '_%'
),
own_methods AS (
  SELECT cm.method_symbol_id,
         cm.method_qualname,
         cm.class_file_id
  FROM class_methods cm
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM class_methods other_m
    WHERE other_m.class_file_id = cm.class_file_id
      AND other_m.method_qualname = cm.method_qualname
      AND other_m.method_symbol_id != cm.method_symbol_id
  )
),
public_own_methods AS (
  SELECT method_symbol_id,
         method_qualname AS method_name,
         class_file_id AS class_symbol_id
  FROM own_methods
  WHERE method_qualname NOT LIKE '_%'
)
SELECT class_symbol_id,
       method_name
FROM public_own_methods
ORDER BY class_symbol_id,
       method_name;
